items_missed: No 'How are you today?', no agenda statement, no 'sound good?' confirmation
Customer's name never asked for — only inferred from his email address at the very end ('I'm assuming your first name is Jonathan')
Asked the target date but never checked or confirmed availability for it

Almost no probing beyond zips and bedroom count — no floor or stairs at either end, no elevator/parking/access, no packing needs, no box count, no specialty items, no additional stops or storage, no moving-stressors question
Said 'that gets you everything that is needed' but never itemized what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no 'no hidden fees' pitch
No No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee
Clock partially covered — explained when the rate starts but skipped the 2.5-hour minimum and the 15-minute prorated increments
No Save Your Ass prep speech at all — a long-distance move where prep has the biggest dollar impact
No booking attempt — closed with the passive 'if you wanna move forward with booking anything, give us a callback'
No bolded email details list, no 'reply with any corrections', no hours
Customer's joke ('it'd be kind of weird if my last name was Jonathan') went unreturned with a flat 'Awesome'
top_strength: Excellent handling of the long-distance pricing structure. She laid out weekday vs. weekend tiers ($208/hr Mon-Thu, $222 weekend), explained the $960 transportation fee, and then proactively surfaced the overnight-crew tradeoff ($1,200 one-day vs. $960 split over two days) before the customer asked. She also checked in mid-explanation — 'I wanna pause, any questions so far? I know I'm kinda throwing a lot at you' — and cleanly answered his follow-up about when the clock starts.
coaching_note: Even on a 'preliminary info' call, run the probe questions — she quoted a two-mover crew and a full-day estimate for a Buda-to-Fort Worth move without knowing the apartment floor, elevator access, box count, or whether packing was needed, which is exactly how a quote drifts outside the 20% band. Capture the name at the top of the call, not from the email spelling at the end.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and pleasant with a good mid-call check-in and a warm close, but largely transactional — no name use until the last minute and the customer's one attempt at humor got a generic 'Awesome' in return.
